title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
moral: Always tell the truth, about big things and little things, so that people can believe you when it matters most; and when you make a mistake, saying sorry and telling the truth is the first step back.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Once upon a time, in a little village tucked between green hills, lived a boy called Finn.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Finn lived with his Grandma Rosie, who baked the warmest, softest bread in the whole village.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Every morning the village woke up slowly. Farmer Ben fed his hens, Grandma Rosie opened her bakery, and Finn's friend Lena skipped across the square.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: And every morning, Finn had a very important job.

lines.speaker: ROSIE
lines.performance_direction: warm, loving grandmother
lines.text: Good morning, Finn. Are you ready to look after the sheep today?

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: bright, eager, about eight years old
lines.text: Yes, Grandma! I'll take them up the hill to the sweet green grass.

lines.speaker: ROSIE
lines.performance_direction: warm, then serious and clear
lines.text: Good boy. And remember: if a wolf ever comes, you shout wolf as loud as you can, and we will all come running to help.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: cheerful, a promise
lines.text: I'll remember, Grandma.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: So Finn led the sheep up the winding path to the top of the hill. There were five fluffy sheep, and one little lamb called Daisy, who had a white heart on her nose.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: counting happily, sing-song
lines.text: One, two, three, four, five sheep... and Daisy makes six. Everybody's here!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Daisy was Finn's favourite. She followed him everywhere and nuzzled his hand.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, lazy and slow
lines.text: The sheep munched the grass. Munch, munch, munch. The clouds drifted by. The sun climbed higher.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: bored, sighing, a little whiny
lines.text: Oh, this is so boring. Nothing ever happens up here.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Finn sat on the big grey rock and sighed. Then he had an idea. It was not a very good idea.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: mischievous, whispering to himself
lines.text: I know! I'll play a trick. That will make things exciting!

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: shouting loudly, pretending to be scared
lines.text: Wolf! Wolf! A wolf is chasing the sheep!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, quick
lines.text: Down in the village, everyone stopped what they were doing, and they ran up the hill path as fast as they could.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: But when they reached the top, there was no wolf at all. Just the sheep, munching grass, and Finn, rolling on the grass with laughter.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: laughing, cheeky
lines.text: Ha ha! There's no wolf! I tricked you!

lines.speaker: BEN
lines.performance_direction: big, deep, kind but cross
lines.text: Finn, that's not funny. We left our work to help you.

lines.speaker: ROSIE
lines.performance_direction: gentle, serious, disappointed
lines.text: A shout for help is not a joke, Finn. Please don't do that again.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: The villagers walked back down the hill, shaking their heads.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: The next day, Finn was on the hill again. And again, he felt bored.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: mischievous, giggling
lines.text: Last time was so funny. I'll do it one more time.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: shouting, fake panic
lines.text: Wolf! Wolf! Help, help, the wolf is here!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Once again, the villagers ran up the hill, puffing and panting.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: And once again, there was no wolf. Only Finn, giggling behind the big grey rock.

lines.speaker: LENA
lines.performance_direction: a girl of nine, upset, hurt
lines.text: Finn! You scared us! I thought the sheep were in danger!

lines.speaker: BEN
lines.performance_direction: slow, serious, not shouting
lines.text: Finn, if you keep crying wolf when there is no wolf, nobody will believe you when there really is one.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, quiet
lines.text: The villagers went home, and this time they were not just cross. They were sad.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Finn watched them go. For a moment, his tummy felt a little funny, but he shrugged and looked away.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: That evening, as the sun began to set and the sky turned orange and pink, something moved at the edge of the dark woods.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, a little suspense, never scary
lines.text: It was a wolf. A real one. He was long and grey, with a big bushy tail and a very hungry tummy.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: The wolf crept closer, licking his lips and looking at the fluffy sheep.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: frightened, a whisper
lines.text: Oh no. Oh no! That's a real wolf!

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: shouting with all his might, truly scared, begging
lines.text: Wolf! Wolf! Please help! There really is a wolf this time!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Down in the village, the villagers heard Finn shouting.

lines.speaker: BEN
lines.performance_direction: tired, shaking his head
lines.text: Not again. That boy is playing another trick.

lines.speaker: LENA
lines.performance_direction: unsure, worried
lines.text: Should we go, Grandma Rosie?

lines.speaker: ROSIE
lines.performance_direction: sad, torn
lines.text: I don't know, Lena. I want to believe him. But he has fooled us twice.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, sad and slow
lines.text: And so, nobody came.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, fast, never scary
lines.text: The wolf leapt toward the flock. The sheep bleated and scattered in every direction, running into the woods to hide.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Finn was frightened, but he was brave. He ran to the old bell on the hill and rang it with all his might.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: playful sound words, ringing and loud
lines.text: Clang! Clang! Clang!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, relieved
lines.text: The loud clanging startled the wolf. He tucked his tail between his legs and ran back into the woods, far, far away.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, quiet
lines.text: The wolf was gone. But so were the sheep.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: calling, worried
lines.text: Daisy? Daisy! Where are you? Where is everybody?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, tender
lines.text: The hill was empty and quiet. Finn sat down on the grass, and big tears rolled down his cheeks.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: crying softly, sorry
lines.text: This is all my fault. If I hadn't told those fibs, everyone would have come.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Finn ran all the way down to the village as fast as his legs could carry him.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: breathless, upset, honest
lines.text: Grandma! The wolf came, a real wolf! I rang the bell and he ran away, but the sheep ran into the woods, and Daisy is lost!

lines.speaker: BEN
lines.performance_direction: doubtful, gentle
lines.text: Is this another trick, Finn?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Grandma Rosie looked at Finn's face. She saw his real tears, and she knelt down beside him.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: sincere, sorry, through tears
lines.text: It's not a trick. I'm so sorry I told fibs before. I won't ever do it again. This time, it's true.

lines.speaker: ROSIE
lines.performance_direction: warm, decisive, kind
lines.text: I believe you, Finn. Come on, everyone. Let's find those sheep.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: So the whole village went out to the edge of the woods, just as the first stars began to twinkle.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: They searched behind the bushes and under the ferns, calling softly.

lines.speaker: LENA
lines.performance_direction: excited, happy
lines.text: Here's one! And another!

lines.speaker: BEN
lines.performance_direction: pleased, deep
lines.text: Three more over here!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: One, two, three, four, five sheep were found. But where was Daisy?

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: calling, hopeful
lines.text: Daisy! Daisy, where are you?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, soft
lines.text: Then, from under a big leafy bush, came a tiny sound. Baa.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: overjoyed, relieved
lines.text: Daisy! There you are!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Finn hugged Daisy tight, and Daisy nuzzled his cheek.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Back home, Grandma Rosie sat with Finn on the step of the little bakery, with Daisy curled up at his feet.

lines.speaker: ROSIE
lines.performance_direction: wise, gentle, like a bedtime talk
lines.text: Finn, trust is like a tower of blocks. Every time you tell the truth, you add a block, and the tower grows tall and strong.

lines.speaker: ROSIE
lines.performance_direction: gentle, honest
lines.text: But every fib knocks some blocks down. And it takes a long, long time to build the tower up again.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: small voice, thoughtful
lines.text: I knocked my tower down, didn't I?

lines.speaker: ROSIE
lines.performance_direction: kind, encouraging
lines.text: A little. But you told the truth tonight, and that was a very good block to start with.

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: determined, hopeful
lines.text: Then I'll build it up again. One true word at a time.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: From that day on, Finn always told the truth, about big things and little things.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Each morning he led the sheep up the hill, and Daisy trotted right beside him.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: And if he ever felt bored, he played games that didn't fool anybody, like counting clouds, or teaching Daisy to dance.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling
lines.text: Little by little, block by block, the villagers learned to trust Finn again.

lines.speaker: LENA
lines.performance_direction: cheerful, friendly
lines.text: Good morning, Finn! How are the sheep today?

lines.speaker: FINN
lines.performance_direction: happy, proud, honest
lines.text: All six of them are happy and safe. And that's the truth!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, the moral, slow and clear
lines.text: Because when you always tell the truth, people will believe you when it matters most.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.performance_direction: warm, gentle storyteller for small children, unhurried, smiling, closing
lines.text: The end.
